coverage.notes: SEL: MDE publishes a 'Minnesota SEL Framework': five competencies (named like CASEL's) with 14 learning goals and grade-band benchmarks (K-3, 4-5, 6-8, 9-12), sample activities and links to MN academic standards. The MDE documents call the activities suggestions; I found no statement that these are adopted or required standards, so 'guidance_only'. MDE's SEL landing page (education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/safe/social/) returned a Radware 'verifying your browser' page and I did not try to get around it, so current status wording and any newer revision were NOT checked. Portrait of a Graduate: no official MDE statewide portrait found in web searches (only a Minnesota Rural Education Association district-support program, not a state agency effort); MDE's site could not be browsed, so 'unknown', not 'none'. Reviewer: open the MDE SEL page in a normal browser to confirm.

frameworks.name: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
frameworks.notes: Read from MDE PDFs (metadata dates Feb-Mar 2018) under https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/groups/educ/documents/hiddencontent/bwrl/mdcz/~edisp/ : mde073492 Self-Awareness (3 goals), mde073494 Self-Management (2), mde073495 Relationship Skills (3), mde073514 Social Awareness (4). No Responsible Decision-Making benchmark PDF found; its 2 goals come from MDE's 2-page 'Handout 2b: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals' (https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/groups/educ/documents/basic/cm9k/mdq2/~edisp/prod046200.pdf), which also matches the other 12 goals. Items are learning goals, not per-grade benchmarks. Codes (SA-1, SM-2...) are short stable codes I made up; MDE numbers goals 1-4 within each competency. caselCompetency = the competency MDE files each goal under. Adoption year blank. The 2018 documents may be superseded; please check for a newer version.

items.title: Awareness and understanding of own emotions
items.summary: Recognize, label and understand one's own emotions.

items.title: Awareness of strengths, challenges, aspirations and assets
items.summary: Understand one's strengths, challenges and goals, including cultural, linguistic and community assets.

items.title: Awareness of personal rights and responsibilities
items.summary: Understand one's own rights and responsibilities.

items.title: Manage and express emotions, thoughts, impulses and stress
items.summary: Use effective skills to manage and express emotions, thoughts, impulses and stress.

items.title: Set, monitor, adapt, achieve and evaluate goals
items.summary: Use skills to set goals, track progress, adjust, reach them and judge the results.

items.title: Awareness of and empathy for individuals across cultures
items.summary: Show awareness of and empathy for other people's emotions, experiences and perspectives through a cross-cultural lens.

items.title: Awareness and respect of groups and their cultures
items.summary: Show awareness and respect for groups and their cultures, languages, identities, traditions, values and histories.

items.title: How individuals and groups cooperate toward common goals
items.summary: Understand how people and groups work together toward shared goals and ideals.

items.title: Awareness of external supports
items.summary: Know what outside supports exist and when they are needed.

items.title: Communication and social skills to interact effectively
items.summary: Use a range of communication and social skills to interact well with others.

items.title: Approaches to addressing interpersonal conflict
items.summary: Identify and use approaches for handling conflict between people.

items.title: Consider ethical standards, norms and safety in decisions
items.summary: Weigh ethical standards, social and community norms and safety concerns when making decisions.

items.title: Apply and evaluate decision-making skills
items.summary: Use and evaluate decision-making skills across a variety of situations.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

target.title: Stay in Control of Your Spirit - Lesson Plan 10 - 23 - #155 - MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Feelings Detective" (tagged self-awareness). FNE's catalog description: "Notice real cues in a scene, then pick every feeling that plausibly fits." Covers naming what someone feels from real cues; it does not by itself connect those feelings to the player's own actions.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Emotional Intelligence" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." The theme names understanding emotions and self-awareness. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Take Responsibility for Your Growth" (series: Responsibility & Ownership; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that support from teachers, family, and friends matters, but no one can grow for them. They will learn that personal growth happens when they choose effort, practice, better responses, and steady learning, even when it feels ..." Covers personal responsibility for one's own growth. Limit: Responsibilities only; the goal also covers personal rights, which FNE does not address.

target.title: Take Responsibility for Your Growth - Lesson Plan 5 - 21 - #44_MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Leadership & Responsibility" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "What leadership looks like in a classroom, on a team, and in a community. Students explore ownership, initiative, accountability, and what it means to lead from any position." The theme names ownership and accountability. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Calm Is A Super Power" (series: Emotional Strength; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that calm is strength under control. They will learn to identify situations that may trigger quick reactions, practice habits that support self-control, and recognize how calm responses can improve decisions, relationships, and daily ..." The lesson teaches spotting triggers and practising habits that interrupt impulsive reactions, matching the self-regulation skill.

target.title: Calm Is A Super Power - Lesson Plan 8 - 31 - #116 - MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Pause Before You Escalate" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that a conflict is escalating, practice a short pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful response that helps move the situation toward an answer." Teaches a short pause-and-reset routine before responding, matching the skill of managing emotions and behaviour.

target.title: Pause Before You Escalate - Lesson Plan 10 - 19 - #151 - MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Calm Down Corner" (tagged self-management). FNE's catalog description: "Listen to a frustrating moment, then pick what would help you feel calm." Students pick what would help them calm down after a frustrating moment, which practises the same strategy-choosing skill.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Emotional Intelligence" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Growth Requires Repetition" (series: Personal Growth in Action; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will explain why repetition supports growth, identify one skill or habit they want to strengthen, recognize how tracking and feedback improve practice, and choose one repeated action that supports progress." Students choose a skill to strengthen, track it and adjust with feedback, which is goal-setting and monitoring. Limit: Goals are personal habits; it does not cover career or post-graduation planning.

target.title: Growth Requires Repetition - Lesson Plan 9 - 21 - #131 - MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals

FNE's stated objective: "Learners will explain how reflection supports growth, identify one useful lesson from a recent experience, and choose one present action that applies that learning in a constructive way." Turns reflection on a recent experience into one present action; supports reviewing and adjusting.

target.title: Carry Yesterday’s Growth Forward - Lesson Plan 9 - 8 - #122 - MS

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Sharing Circle" (tagged social awareness and relationship skills). FNE's catalog description: "Listen to what happened, then pick the kind thing to do." Students listen to what happened to someone and choose the kind response, which practises noticing another person's experience. Limit: Everyday kindness scenarios; does not teach perspective-taking across cultures or backgrounds.

alignments.framework: Minnesota SEL Framework: Competencies and Learning Goals

FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that sharing credit helps build trust, respect, humility, and stronger teamwork. They will learn that every helpful part matters, including listening, encouraging, practicing, helping quietly, offering ideas, and doing their part." Teaches that helping, listening and doing one's part all count toward a team's success. Limit: Classroom-scale teamwork; not structured collaborative problem-solving.

FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that encouragement is a respectful choice that helps strengthen classrooms, teams, families, and communities. They will learn to notice effort, speak with kindness, remind others they can keep going, and use their words to build ..." Teaches encouraging others so classrooms and teams grow stronger. Limit: Encouragement rather than shared problem-solving.
